newsitem.title: UK: Around 30 survive Ethiopian airline crash - witness.
newsitem.headline: Around 30 survive Ethiopian airline crash - witness.

text.p: At least 30 people appear to have survived the crash of a hijacked Ethiopian aircraft into the sea near the Comoro Islands on Saturday, an eyewitness told BBC World Service.

"We've got survivors. They are in hospital close to the hotel. At the last information there are about 30 survivors," said Frederick Chretien, manager of sea-front hotel near the crash site. About 100 bodies had been recovered, he added.
Chretien told BBC World Service radio by telephone that one of the survivors had spoken of seeing two hijackers on board the plane.
He said it was thought two bombs being carried by the hijackers were still on board the crashed aircraft but there was no confirmation.
"Apparently there are two bombs still in the aircraft and we are waiting for the French forces to investigate for the two bombs," he said.

Chretien is manager of the Hotel Le Galawa in the Comoros, directly opposite the site where the plane carrying about 178 passengers and crew crashed after being hijacked while on route from Addis Ababa to Nairobi in Kenya.
